summary: The study investigates the nucleation and growth of InGaZnO thin films using spatial atmospheric atomic layer deposition (S-ALD). The films are deposited by coinjecting metal precursors (DEZ, TMIn, TEGa) and water, with the metal composition controlled by varying the flow rates of TMIn and TEGa. The films are used as active channels in thin-film transistors (TFTs), and the influence of In and Ga cations on the electrical characteristics of the TFTs is studied. The results show that the films can be grown with a high deposition rate and good uniformity, and the electrical properties are influenced by the metal composition.
evidence: We have investigated the nucleation and growth of InGaZnO thin films by spatial atmospheric atomic layer deposition. Diethyl zinc (DEZ), trimethyl indium (TMIn), triethyl gallium (TEGa), and water were used as Zn, In, Ga and oxygen precursors, respectively. The vaporized metal precursors have been coinjected in the reactor. The metal composition of InGaZnO has been controlled by varying the TMIn or TEGa flow to the reactor, for a given DEZ flow and exposure time. The use of these films as the active channel in TFTs has been demonstrated and the influence of In and Ga cations on the electrical characteristics of the TFTs has been studied.
